In this training, you will learn how to use Presentation mode.
The canvas contains slides about green tea and its preparation. Presentation frames surround the slides. Show or hide them using the eye icon in the upper-right corner.
Visible frames stay on top and can be selected. To edit or move objects inside a visible frame, use the Direct Select tool (A). Select a frame to set its label, presentation order, and aspect ratio (16:9, 4:3, or free).
Open the Presentation canvas with the button next to the eye icon, then select Start frame presentation. During the presentation, you can dim the surrounding area, choose animated or instant frame transitions, zoom, pan, and use the Left and Right Arrow keys to change slides.
Select the pencil icon to return to edit mode.

Need focus? Matcha. Want something fresh? Sencha. Looking for deep umami? Gyokuro. Want a gentle evening cup? Hojicha. Genmaicha is a comforting choice with food, while Kukicha is a soft, easy cup for any time of day.

“Gyokuro is shaded longer for sweetness and umami; Hojicha is roasted for warmth and nuttiness; Genmaicha is blended with toasted rice; Kukicha uses stems for a light sweetness. Each tea offers a different balance of freshness, roast, texture, and caffeine.”
“Sencha grows in sunlight. Steaming keeps the leaves green and fresh. It is Japan's classic everyday green tea. Its clean, grassy character can range from lightly sweet to pleasantly astringent.”
“Sunlight or shade; steamed or roasted; loose leaf or powder; pure tea or blended with rice. These choices shape whether a tea tastes grassy, toasted, sweet, rich, or light.”
The Four Choices That Change Everything

“All of these begin as Camellia sinensis. Sunlight, shade, steam, roasting, and grinding create different teas. Small changes in growing and processing create strikingly different colors, aromas, and flavors.”

“Japan makes many teas from the same plant. The difference is what happens after the leaves are picked. Matcha is made from shade-grown leaves that are ground into a fine powder, while most other teas are brewed from leaves.”
Matcha Is Green Tea. But Not All Green Tea Is Matcha.
Contains: Presentation Frames, Presentation Canvas, Dimming, Gliding
